title: VEs, CSCEs and expired licenses
blurb: Who can be a Volunteer Examiner, how a CSCE and the AG suffix work, expired-license credit, and remote operation.

G1D01.why: Anyone who can show they once held a **General, Advanced or Extra** license that was not revoked gets partial element credit.
G1D01.trap: No 5 to 15 year window, and foreign licenses do not count.

G1D02.why: A General-class VE may administer **Technician** exams only.
G1D02.trap: General and Extra exams need higher-class VEs.

G1D03.why: With an unexpired CSCE you may use **any General or Technician segment**, including 30 m and 60 m.
G1D03.trap: You need not wait for the database or a fee receipt.

G1D04.why: A Technician exam needs **at least three** VEs, each General class or higher.
G1D04.trap: Two VEs is too few, and Technician VEs cannot examine.

G1D05.why: Operating a US station remotely from abroad needs the **US operator/primary license**. No special permit is required.

G1D06.why: Until the upgrade shows in the database, add **AG** whenever you use General privileges.
G1D06.trap: AG is for General segments, not Technician ones.

G1D07.trap: The FCC licenses operators, but VECs accredit examiners.

G1D08.why: A non-US citizen may be a VE if they hold an **FCC General or higher** license.

G1D09.why: A CSCE is valid for exam element credit for **365 days**.

G1D11.why: After the grace period, show proof of the expired grant and **pass the current Element 2** (Technician) exam.

G1D12.why: When controlling a foreign station remotely, **only that country's rules** apply.
G1D12.trap: Where you sit does not set the rules, where the station is does.
